title: Insect Venom
paragraphs: Shield…80%
That island is Nanatsuretsu Island, isn’t it? The Rival scattered the reincarnated ones all over the island, created an inescapable barrier around it, and then brought them back to consciousness.
“Ugh… uuugh… W-where am I!? What’s with this collar!?”

And just like that, the reincarnated ones regained consciousness as if on cue and encountered other reincarnated ones who had woken up at the same time. Every single one of them is wearing a collar. It seems they’ve all gone through the motions of introducing themselves, at least superficially. They gave their names and each claimed to be an “adventurer.” Don’t you think there are way too many of them calling themselves adventurers? Isn’t there a more sensible way to introduce yourself?
“You’re the one who brought us here… no, wait. Who the hell are those Filolial Mask guys?! Did you guys order them to do this? Huh!?”
“Who the hell is that guy! I was just out on a normal adventure when I got attacked by a bunch of guys calling themselves the ‘Dark Holy Heroes’!”

By the way, we know this guy was actually raiding the Adventurers’ Guild under the guise of a “normal adventure.” Apparently, he was trying to take control of the guild by threatening the branch leader with force. As for the other guy, he’s said to have a mountain of charges against him, including brainwashing children at an orphanage or something like that. Sure enough, the pig was rounded up, and the man had a slave mark branded onto him.
“So what the hell is this all about? Dragging us to a place like this…”
They started sizing each other up while pretending to be nonchalant. Objectively speaking, their acting is so obviously fake it’s practically screaming ‘lie.’
“And what’s with this collar! It’s so tight!”
“Wait, my level’s down to 1! You’ve got to be kidding me! Ugh… I can’t muster any strength.”
It seems they reset their levels the moment they were taken away.
“So, where the hell is this place, anyway…”
The reincarnated ones looked around.
“A forest… and a coastline?”
Just as they were having this exchange, a silhouette appeared in the sky. The reincarnated heroes looked up at the sky.
“You all… you know who I am, right? That’s right. It’s me.”
“Ah, it’s you!”
You can’t tell who it is at all from that silhouette. Despite that, the reincarnated heroes look as if they know exactly who it is.
“You were defeated by the Hero. But don’t worry. I’ve used my power to transport you to a different location.”
“Oh…”
They all let out sighs of relief. They’re looking completely clueless, aren’t they?
“The heroes’ power is immense. Defeating them is no easy feat… Though it pains me greatly, among you here—”
“Ah, I get it! It’s a battle royale! Dieeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee!”
Before she could even finish speaking, one reincarnated person used a rusty weapon lying nearby to launch a surprise attack and strike another. What on earth is that guy doing all of a sudden?
“You bastard! Gah—!?”
Although he was somewhat prepared for the sudden ambush, he couldn’t react fast enough, and the blow shattered the victim’s skull, sending him crashing to the ground.

“Haha! I did it! This counts, right? You’re going to grant me a cheat ability that lets me take down those guys by reducing their numbers, aren’t you!?　Since it’s a first kill, I’ll get an amazing ability, right!?”

So said the blood-soaked, jump-to-conclusions reincarnated person, shouting triumphantly toward the sky. What exactly is a “first kill”? It’s completely baffling why he thought he’d get an amazing ability just for committing the first murder. These people really do say the most incomprehensible things.
“Let’s punish those who won’t listen.”
“Huh!? Gya—”

Beep, beep! The collar lit up, and the blood-soaked, hasty reincarnated person was blown to bits. The explosive device built into the collar had detonated. Incidentally, I hear it was a collar developed by Zeltoble. What on earth is that thing used for? If you want to issue forced commands, wouldn’t a slave mark suffice? Even Zeltoble doesn’t seem to have a clue.
“I’ve punished the fools who didn’t listen.”

There was a slight sigh mixed in there. By the way, there were multiple explosions. That reincarnated person was just pretending to be reasonable. The reincarnated people seemed to gasp as they looked at the fool and the remains of the victim.

“Let’s continue. From now on, you’ll have to fight each other until only one of you remains. However, I haven’t given permission to fight yet. First, you have one hour to gather the weapons scattered across the island. Also, it’s impossible to leave the island.”

That’s more or less how the reincarnated people ended up fighting each other. It’s incredibly haphazard. But, as if they’d understood the rules, they glared at one another, then scattered across the island, and began killing each other the moment the signal to start sounded one hour later.

At first glance, there were certainly some dramatic moments—like them trying to cooperate to survive—but every single one of them was just sizing each other up, and it seemed they couldn’t coordinate properly at all. In the end, a few resourceful ones remained, and after spending several days on the island, the number was whittled down to the very last person.
“Ha ha! I did it! I’m the strongest! I did it!”
“Yes, you’re the last one standing. That was a filthy fight—far removed from what it means to be human, worse even than monsters or Beastmen.”
“Ha! What are you talking about! I survived thanks to my cunning! Come on! Hurry up and grant me that awesome cheat!”
“Then shall I grant it?”
A beeping sound rang out…
“What!?　Hey! What the hell are you playing at! You’re kidding me—”

Boom! A loud explosion rang out. The last reincarnator has gone to the afterlife in a most pitiful manner. By the way, this collar is rigged with a bomb planted by Rival that even attacks the soul, so once you die, your soul vanishes too.
“Seriously… I was forced to supervise this, but it makes me want to puke.”
“Why are we being dragged into this, anyway?”
“It’s a black-market movie produced by Zeltoble. Apparently, it’s a reincarnated warrior battle.”

It seems Zeltoble’s black-market guild made an offer to a Rival who struck it rich with a movie using Takt, launching this project to entrust them with disposing of the reincarnated warriors. They say it’s a battle royale reusing the Seven Rifts Island. Something about it becoming entertainment for the world’s underworld, or so they say. “Maybe we’ve just discovered the real Trash here. ‘Now, blow it up! HAHAHA!’—that’s probably what they’re saying.” It seems the reincarnated individuals captured by the Hero are being consumed one after another in these countless games.
“No matter how much we’re forced to kill each other, I wish they’d resist with a little more conscience,”
Rival says gloomily.

“Even though the scale may differ, the heroes were forced to do this too… but what matters is the weight of the burden they carry. These guys… Naofumi, at least, is trying to find a way to resist this fate. Despite that, those who willingly kill each other are just scum.”
“Ah, it’s the Crimson Swine himself. Father mentioned there were others like him.”
“No matter where you go, there are always those tainted by similar filthy thoughts. It’s truly lamentable.”

Rival’s sigh is unnecessarily loud. With that haughty attitude, he’s trying to say you’re one of them, isn’t he? Oh? It feels like Ren and Itsuki—back when we first headed to Ren and Faubrey in the first world—are pointing at me and saying, “You’re the one who said that!”… but I’m probably just imagining things! I’m just cleaning up after you lot alongside Rival, you know.
“Anyway, we’ve almost finished rooting out all the reincarnated ones, so this world has, for the time being, become peaceful.”
Rival says this with a “Oh, well” sort of expression, as if the job were done.

And so, the handling of the reincarnated individuals progressed steadily, and the world moved closer to peace. There were various behind-the-scenes maneuvers by Rival, but for the most part, things are proceeding without a hitch. Since there’s no revival of the Four Spirits or anything like that, all that’s left is to be patient until this wave subsides.

Eventually, Big Sister returned from her training alongside Éclair and Leiska. Ah, Éclair’s looking quite plain today. Isn’t it about time the big sisters took on the challenge to become holders of the Seven Star Weapons? I hear Leiska has also shown her talent and is now a reliable partner to Fleon and Itsuki.

In any case, since they’ve thoroughly completed their training, the big sisters have decided to undergo a Class Up through Limit Break. The old woman of the Hengen Muso Style also performed the Limit Break on them. My Father and I were there to witness it. Ah, right—Filo-tan and my Finacée had already gone through it.
“Rafu.”
“Alright, now it’s Raphtalia’s turn.”
“Y-yes… that’s right, but Naofumi-sama? Could you please stop petting Raph-chan nonstop already…?”
My Father seems to genuinely love the Rafu species.
“Don’t worry about it.”
“Sigh…”
“Oh my—”
My Big Sister’s Big Sister is also here to witness my Big Sister’s Limit Break Class Up. She’s watching my Big Sister—who’s trying to scold her—with a warm, amused smile.
“For a Limit Break Class Up, isn’t there some kind of method using that silly strand of hair Fitoria gave you?”
“At least, it’s not within Gaelion and the Spear Hero’s knowledge.”
I can’t say for certain that it doesn’t exist, though.
“I see. Well, it’s Raphtalia’s choice, after all. Raphtalia, make sure to decide on your own potential.”
“Rafu—”

My Father said this while petting the Rafu. He seems a little disappointed. However, the rhythm of his voice was slightly different from how it’s been in previous loops. He seems to be expecting something, but the fact that he doesn’t say it outright is probably his own way of being kind.
“Go for it, Rafu! I’m rooting for you, Kou!”
Kou cheers on his Big Sister. By the way, Kou gets along great with the Raph breed, too, of course!
“O-okay…”
“I wonder if Big Sister’s recommendation is based on cleaning ability or something? Raphtalia, you do love to keep things clean, don’t you?”
“I suppose that’s fine if that’s what Raphtalia wants…”
“Clean! Clean! Is Raph going to get even better at cleaning? Does that mean she’ll be able to groom Kou’s fur faster, too?”
“Why would that happen…?”
Sighing, Big Sister responds to her older sister, Father, and Kou’s comments in a tone of exasperation.
“I’ll check it out for now.”
“So, the ritual is about to begin!”

And so, the Rival begins the Class Up ritual to break through her limits and level up. Naturally, the Four Holy Weapons and the Seven Star Weapons are essential for performing the ritual. The Rival began chanting Magic. Then, using the Dragon Hourglass, she performed the ritual, and light began to gather around Big Sister.
“Rafu!”
“Ah!”
Just then, the Rafu-species leapt right out of Father’s hand and dashed toward Big Sister. There was a “boom,” and a cloud of smoke swirled up as the light scattered.
“Cough, cough! W-what just…”
“Raph!”
When the smoke cleared, Big Sister was coughing, and the Raph Seed was standing proudly with its chest puffed out, facing us.
“Oh my… really?”
My Rival let out a cry of surprise at this unexpected accident.
“Raph, are you okay?”
Kou said, looking at both my Big Sister and the Raph-type.
“Hmm… It looks like the Class Up is complete. Raphtalia, what did you choose?”
“No, just as I was about to choose, Raph-chan rushed in and, just like with Filo’s Class Up, went ahead and chose something on her own.”
“Raph-chan, you shouldn’t just do things like that on your own.”
Even my Father scolded the Raph-type while still praising her.
“Raph?”
As if asking, “Did I mess up?”, the Raph-species tilted her little head and looked back and forth between my Father and Big Sister.
“Choosing on your own like that… Should we reset it?”
“Leave the leveling up to me! With Naofumi-chan and me here, we’ll catch up in no time!”
“Ah, right—the monsters on the ocean floor give as much EXP as those on Cal Mira Island… That’s a good option, too.”

That’s the kind of leveling Big Sister excels at. I’ve gotten the hang of it in Submarine Mode, too. Though diving with Filolial-sama is a bit tricky, so I’ll need to do some research. If I could use water magic like Ren or my Finacée, I could level up Filolial-sama and the others safely. It’s definitely a hassle to constantly break the surface with a spear just to hunt on the ocean floor… Burning the ocean with “Prominence” to make it evaporate is another option. When I tried to do that later, my Father scolded me, saying, “There’s a hero who set the ocean on fire in the opening sequence, but don’t actually do it!”
“Hmm… That said, it’s not like I had anything specific I wanted to do, so maybe I’ll check a few things first…”
As she said that, my older sister seemed to be checking her own stats.
“Everything’s improved overall. If anything, my Magical Power has gone up a bit…”
“Oh? Raphtalia-chan.”
My older sister stared intently at Raphtalia and checked her, almost as if giving her a light physical exam.
“Is it just my imagination? I think you’re probably able to transform into a Beastman now.”
